title: Password Generator
story: 'password123' is NOT a good password. A strong password is random, long, and mixes letters, numbers, and symbols. Instead of thinking one up (humans are terrible at randomness), let your code generate cryptographically-sound passwords.
why: Password generation teaches random selection from character sets, configurable composition rules, and building strings from randomized components.
analogy: Mixing paint colors: lowercase letters are blue, uppercase are red, digits are yellow, symbols are green. Your password generator dips from each can randomly, creating a unique, unpredictable color blend every time. No two passwords are ever the same.
try_it: Add a guarantee that the password contains at least one of each selected character type (upper, digit, symbol). Re-generate until the guarantee is met. Add a password strength meter that rates passwords 'Weak', 'Medium', 'Strong' based on length and character variety.
tips: Always include lowercase — it's the baseline
Use a simple LCG (Linear Congruential Generator) for random numbers
Password strength = length × character set diversity
common_mistakes: Generating from only lowercase — trivially crackable
Using predictable seed — every run produces the same password
Making passwords too short — 8 chars minimum, 12+ recommended
